issue.title: feat: stripe connection free lists over multiple shards
issue.body:
To reduce mutex contention on busy applications, split lists of free connections into multiple shards each with their own mutex. Shards are picked based on a hash of the server address. By default, only a single shard is used preserving the existing behavior.

#### Note to reviewers

Most of the changes in `memcache_test.go` are cleanup so that we are explicitly starting and stopping servers for tests instead of relying on an ambient server running locally or in the CI runner.

comment.body: I think we can go this way, but also food for thought: why not a map with server address as key and free connections as list? We'd need to read-lock the map to take the free address list, but write-locks on it should be very unfrequent so that's an almost free operation, and then the contention would be limited to just one server.
This allocates a byte slice and this is a hot path, can we find a better approach? Also, I think xxhash is faster.
Shards len is a power of two, but runtime doesn't know that so `%` is going to be a usual modulo operation. It's not a big deal but also easy to optimize.

issue.title: feat: add --inject-label flag to apply, diff, show and export
issue.body:
Adds a repeatable `--inject-label key=value` flag to `tk apply`, `diff`, `show` and `export`.

The flag sets the given label on every rendered resource, overriding any pre-existing value. This makes it easy to identify, in a cluster, which resources a given run touched (e.g. `--inject-label created-by=alice`) without having to edit the Environment's `spec.json`.

It is intentionally distinct from `spec.injectLabels` (the boolean toggling the `tanka.dev/environment` label) and from `spec.resourceDefaults.labels` (which only fills in missing keys). Labels are injected at the single `LoadManifests` chokepoint, so all four commands behave consistently.

issue.title: distributor: don't build the full OTLP parse error message
issue.body:
#### What this PR does

The OTLP translator calls `errors.Join` once per invalid metric, which nests the errors. `otlpMimirConverter.Err()` called `Error()` on the whole chain and only then truncated the message to 1024 bytes. That allocates O(N^2) bytes in the number of invalid metrics.

A request with many metrics that Mimir rejects (for example delta temporality when delta ingestion is disabled) can use a lot of distributor CPU and memory, mostly in GC.

Now the joined errors are walked and the message stops once 1024 bytes have been written. The message returned to the client is the same. With 10k invalid metrics, building the message goes from ~386ms and 3.7GB to ~0.2ms and 670KB.

issue.title: usage-tracker: load snapshots into populated shards a batch at a time
issue.body:
#### What this PR does

A usage-tracker loads the snapshots that the other zone publishes for its partition, and held the shard lock while it put a whole shard snapshot: with 330M series per partition in `mimir-dev-13` that is 5M series and 100 to 200 ms per shard, 64 times every 10 minutes, and every `trackSeries` request of the tenant waited for it. That is where the 10-minute p99 spikes come from once #16892 is deployed: they happen while the other zone's snapshot is being loaded, not while the pod's own snapshot is taken.

`loadSnapshotSeries` now puts 16K series per lock hold into a shard that already has series, about a millisecond, and releases the lock between batches. An empty shard is still filled in one hold, since nothing is tracked in it yet.

Stacked on #16892, to be rebased onto `main` once that merges.

#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes or relates to

Follow-up to #16892.

issue.title: usage-tracker: snapshot tenant shards a chunk at a time
issue.body:
#### What this PR does

Stacked on #16882, which it includes: it will be rebased onto `main` once that one is merged.

The snapshot cloned the keys and data arrays of a tenant shard under the shard lock, so that it could encode the series with the lock released. At 30M series per shard (500M per partition with 16 shards) that is a 514 MB copy, and even with warm buffers the lock is held for 15 ms on an M3 Pro, and longer on amd64. Every `trackSeries` request touches all the shards of the tenant, so each snapshot stalled every request of that tenant once per shard.

`Items()` is replaced by `Iterate()`, which takes the lock for 16K groups at a time (1 MB of keys), copies the series of that chunk to a small scratch, releases the lock, and only then yields them. Series tracking takes the lock in between chunks, so it waits for a fraction of a millisecond at most, whatever the size of the shard. The 514 MB transient clone is gone too. A rehash while iterating moves every series, so `Iterate` detects it through the rehash counter and starts over, and after three restarts it reads the whole map in one lock hold.

The per-tenant series count goes before the series in the snapshot, but with a chunked read it is only known at the end. It is now written as a 10-byte padded uvarint, filled in once the series are written. Uvarint decoders read bytes until one has no continuation bit, so the snapshot format and its readers don't change, and usage-trackers running the previous version read the new snapshots.

#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes or relates to

N/A

#### Checklist

- [x] Tests updated.
- [ ] Documentation added.
- [x] `CHANGELOG.md` updated - the order of entries should be `[CHANGE]`, `[FEATURE]`, `[ENHANCEMENT]`, `[BUGFIX]`. If changelog entry is not needed, please add the `changelog-not-needed` label to the PR.
- [ ] [`about-versioning.md`](https://github.com/grafana/mimir/blob/main/docs/sources/mimir/configure/about-versioning.md) updated with experimental features.

#### Benchmark

`BenchmarkTrackerStoreTrackSeriesDuringSnapshot` (added here) tracks 1K series per call against one tenant while snapshots of that tenant run back to back, and reports the slowest call as `max_ms`. M3 Pro, 16 shards, 3 runs each:

| series per shard | max `trackSeries`, before | max `trackSeries`, after | mean, before | mean, after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1M (16M total) | 1.5 to 2.0 ms | 0.7 to 1.0 ms | 60 to 66 µs | 120 to 130 µs |
| 4M (64M total) | 5.5 to 11 ms | 0.45 to 0.65 ms | 63 to 64 µs | 114 to 136 µs |

The stall no longer grows with the shard: at 30M series per shard the clone held the lock for 15 ms with warm buffers (and for 140 to 230 ms before #16882), a chunk read holds it for a fraction of a millisecond.

The higher mean is an artifact of the benchmark, where a snapshot is always running: the chunked read spends more time under the lock in total than the memcpy of the clone did (about 14 ms per 4M-series shard, spread over 31 holds, against one 2 ms hold), so a tracking call collides with a hold more often. In production a snapshot runs once per `idle-timeout/2`, 10 minutes by default, so that extra time under the lock is about 0.3% of the time.

issue.title: usagetracker: clean up tenantshard v2 groups with 64-bit SWAR
issue.body:
#### What this PR does

`tenantshard/v2.Map.Cleanup` checks every occupied slot with a data-dependent branch, and it runs while it holds the shard lock. This PR checks a whole 8-slot group as one `uint64` instead. Byte-wise subtraction, addition and comparison that never carry into the next byte compute `clock.Minutes.GreaterOrEqualThan` with the same steps as the Go code, and give the same result for every watermark and value. A new test checks all of them.

Previously we checked each element of a group independently, now Cleanup handles 8 groups at a time (64 elements), whose data fills one 64-byte cache line, with one branch per block. A block with nothing to remove is not written. So that there is no tail to handle, the number of groups is now always a multiple of 8. That adds at most 7 groups to a map: the smallest tenants, at about 14 series per tenant shard, go from 4 to 8 groups.

This is an alternative to #16802 without assembly and without the avo dependency. It is plain Go, so it works on every architecture, arm64 included, and the Cleanup loop has no function calls. The group size stays at 8, so Put and Rehash do not change.

It also fixes `BenchmarkMapRehash` (the same commit as in #16802), which passed the number of entries to `rehash` as a number of groups. `BenchmarkMapCleanup` gets cases that look like production churn: a tenant churns 1/3 to 2/3 of its series every 2h, and the watermark moves once a minute, so a cleanup removes 1/360 to 1/180 of the entries, or nothing before the watermark moves again. The old cases, where about 25% expire at once, stay as the corner case.

Results on c7i.2xlarge (Xeon Platinum 8488C), Go 1.26.7, `GOAMD64=v3`, 1M entries per map. The three versions ran alternately on each of two instances, n=5 per instance. Values are instance 1 / instance 2:

| Benchmark | main | #16802 (AVX2) | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cleanup, 25% expired | 8.59 / 8.33ms | 0.70 / 0.67ms (-92%) | 0.88 / 0.81ms (-90%) |
| Cleanup, churn 2/3 per 2h | 4.09 / 3.95ms | 0.83 / 0.79ms (-80%) | 0.96 / 0.91ms (-77%) |
| Cleanup, churn 1/3 per 2h | 4.05 / 3.91ms | 0.71 / 0.68ms (-83%) | 0.90 / 0.85ms (-78%) |
| Cleanup, nothing expires | 4.01 / 3.87ms | 0.44 / 0.42ms (-89%) | 0.63 / 0.59ms (-84%) |
| MapTrackCleanupGarbage | 4.00 / 3.92ms | 2.26 / 2.10ms (-45%) | 1.81 / 1.70ms (-56%) |
| MapRehash, 1M entries | 11.5 / 10.9ms | 16.7 / 14.9ms (+37 to +45%) | 11.1 / 9.9ms (-4 to -9%) |
| MapRehash, 10M entries | 123 / 117ms | 175 / 162ms (+38 to +42%) | 123 / 114ms (0 to -3%) |

With production churn, the AVX2 version is 1.15x to 1.4x faster than this one at Cleanup, because it handles 16 slots per instruction. It makes Rehash about 40% slower and needs assembly. This version does neither.

On an Apple M3 Pro, an earlier version of this PR (one branch per group, before the 8-group blocks) took MapCleanup with 25% expired from 6.7ms to 1.28ms (-81%), and did not change Rehash.

#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes or relates to

Relates to #16802 and #16473

#### Checklist

- [x] Tests updated.
- [ ] Documentation added.
- [x] `CHANGELOG.md` updated - the order of entries should be `[CHANGE]`, `[FEATURE]`, `[ENHANCEMENT]`, `[BUGFIX]`. If changelog entry is not needed, please add the `changelog-not-needed` label to the PR.
- [ ] [`about-versioning.md`](https://github.com/grafana/mimir/blob/main/docs/sources/mimir/configure/about-versioning.md) updated with experimental features.

review.body:
I reviewed this, heavily assisted by Claude. Great stuff!

But I would maybe challenge that this is any better, maintainability-wise, than #16802. I think the concerns raised about assembly apply even more to this heavy bit-twiddling; personally I find the assembly easier to understand than this. The big avo dependency could have been dropped, as the assembly is small and raw enough to be written directly.

All told, both versions would have required of me multiple hours/days of research and paper-and-pencil verification in order to do a non-assisted review or (God forbid) change.
